Home.heroBody: Rock-hewn churches, highland kingdoms, and a landscape unlike anywhere else — shaped into a journey built entirely around you.
Home.brandTitle: A country that rewards slow travel
Home.brandP1: Ethiopia was never conquered by a European power, never fully mapped by outsiders, and has kept its own calendar, its own script and its own church for longer than most nations have existed. Almost nothing here was built for a visitor.
Home.brandP2: We exist to open that country properly, without flattening it into a package tour. Founded and run from Addis Ababa, our team has spent more than ten years building the relationships — with monks, elders, drivers and guides — that make a genuinely private itinerary possible, in ten languages and counting.
Home.brandPrinciple1Rest: before we assume what you want
Home.brandPrinciple2Rest: a single itinerary, never a shelf product
Home.brandPrinciple3Rest: to the communities whose land we visit
Home.destBody: From rock-hewn highlands to a volcanic basin below sea level, each region tells a genuinely different story.
Home.journeysTitle: A starting point, not a fixed itinerary
Home.journeysLede: Each of these routes exists to open a conversation. What you actually travel gets reshaped around your pace and interests.
Home.waysAside: However you like to travel, there's a route built for it — and every one can be reshaped around you.
Home.planTitle: A journey shaped entirely around you
Home.planBody: There's no fixed package to adapt — just a conversation about where you want to go, how you like to travel, and how much time you actually have. From there, a designer builds a route made specifically for that trip, and nothing else.
Home.planPoint1: Planned in Addis, guided by people who live here
Home.planPoint2: One quote up front, no add-ons later
Home.planPoint3: A single point of contact from first email to touchdown home
Home.experiencesTitle: Every way into Ethiopia, one team behind them all
Home.experiencesCard1Title: Stand on the roof of Ethiopia
Home.experiencesCard1Text: Guided ascents of Ras Dashen at 4,550 metres, Bwahit, Tullu Dimtu and Abune Yosef — walking summits with no ropes, just altitude, weather and some of the finest views in Africa.
Home.experiencesCard2Title: Travel with the light, not the clock
Home.experiencesCard2Text: A photographer-guide times every stop to its best hour — Imet Gogo at sunrise, the Lalibela trenches at first light, the salt flats as the heat goes — with portraits only ever taken with consent.
Home.experiencesCard3Text: Dawn on the forest trails of Entoto, around 3,000 metres up, then the highland town of Bekoji — birthplace of Derartu Tulu, Kenenisa Bekele and the Dibaba sisters. Time it to the Great Ethiopian Run in late November.
Home.experiencesCard4Title: Pour injera in a family kitchen
Home.experiencesCard4Text: Learn to pour injera on the mitad, cook the stews that go with it, and share one platter the Ethiopian way — then taste tej, tella and areki on an evening with azmari musicians.

Contact.heroTitle: Start with a conversation, not a form
Contact.heroLede: There is no call centre and no fixed package. Write to us directly and an Addis-based designer replies personally, almost always the same day.
Contact.enquiryBody: An unfinished idea is a fine place to start. We'll come back with the right questions, a route worth considering, and a straight number on what it costs.
Contact.processTitle: From first message to first draft
Contact.processAside: Four steps in total, and nothing is charged until the third one is right.
Contact.step1Title: Tell us the shape of it
Contact.step1Text: One paragraph is plenty. Rough dates, how you like to move, and what you actually want the trip to feel like.
Contact.step2Text: Inside 24 hours, a named designer sends back two or three real options with honest, all-in pricing.
Contact.step3Text: Most itineraries go through two or three drafts. No deposit changes hands until you're genuinely happy with it.
Contact.step4Text: Met at arrival, guided the whole way, with a direct line to your designer open for the length of the trip.
Contact.faqIntro: Straight answers about how planning with us actually works.
Contact.faqA1: An Addis Ababa–based designer usually replies the same day during {hours}. Outside those hours we still monitor urgent messages, and someone on the ground remains reachable once your trip is underway.
Contact.faqQ2: Do I need a finished itinerary before I write?
Contact.faqA2: No. A rough window, how many travellers, and what draws you to Ethiopia is enough. We treat the catalogue routes as starting points and redraw the trip around your pace, altitude comfort and interests.
Contact.faqQ3: When do you take a deposit?
Contact.faqA3: Only after you are happy with a draft itinerary and pricing. There is no obligation for an exploratory conversation, and we will not ask for payment while we are still shaping the trip.
Contact.faqQ4: Can you help with visas and flights?
Contact.faqA4: We advise on Ethiopian e-visa requirements and domestic flight timing, and we book in-country logistics. International flights stay with you or your own agent unless you ask us to arrange something specific.
Contact.faqA5: You write to {company} directly — not a call centre. One named designer follows your enquiry through to departure, with a phone and WhatsApp line open on the ground.

Promises.promise1Title: Run by people who live here
Promises.promise1Text: An Addis Ababa-based team of designers, guides and drivers who have worked as a unit for years — not a distant office booking through a local subcontractor.
Promises.promise2Text: No route on this site is fixed. Every itinerary starts from your pace, your interests and your tolerance for altitude, and is drawn from there.
Promises.promise3Title: Doors that don't open for everyone
Promises.promise3Text: Curators, clergy, archaeologists and artisans who make time outside normal hours, through relationships built over years rather than booking fees.
Promises.promise4Title: One point of contact, start to finish
Promises.promise4Text: A single named designer follows your trip from first enquiry to final departure, with a direct line open for the whole journey.
Promises.contactTitle: What stays true on every trip we run

Tours.heroLede: Every route here is drawn from years on the ground across Ethiopia. Treat them as a draft — the version you travel will be redrawn around you.
Tours.stylesTitle: Choose how you'd like to travel
Tours.stylesAside: Every journey can be private. Pick a style to see the routes built for it.
Tours.collectionAside: Sort by the kind of travel you're after — any route here can be stretched, shortened or joined with another.
Tours.faqIntro: Pricing, fitness, group size and what is included — before you fall in love with a route.
Tours.faqA1: No. Every journey on this site is a private starting point. We reshape days, lodges and pacing around you — most guests end up between two catalogue routes rather than booking one unchanged.
Tours.faqQ2: How does pricing work for tailor-made trips?
Tours.faqA2: Some shorter routes show a from-price; many are quoted individually because lodge availability, domestic flights and group size change the total. We send a clear line-item quote before any deposit.
Tours.faqQ3: What group size do you work with?
Tours.faqA3: Most private trips run for two to eight guests. Solo travellers and larger family groups are welcome — we adjust vehicles, rooms and guiding accordingly.
Tours.faqQ4: How fit do I need to be?
Tours.faqA4: It depends on the route. Historic-route days can stay gentle; Simien and Bale treks need steady walking at altitude. Tell us your comfort level and we will avoid or include the harder legs honestly.
Tours.faqQ5: Do you include domestic flights and park fees?
Tours.faqA5: Inclusions are listed on each tour page. Domestic flights, park fees, guides and most meals are usually included on longer circuits; international flights, visas and travel insurance are not.
Tours.faqA6: Yes on many cultural and city routes. High escarpment treks and the Danakil are better for older teens and adults. We design family pacing and rooming from the first draft.
Tours.ctaTitle: None of these quite fit? Start blank
Tours.ctaText: Most guests actually land somewhere between two of these routes. Describe what you have in mind and a designer will draft it from scratch.
Tours.detailTitleNights: {nights}, designed around the hours that matter
Tours.detailTitleDay: A single day, designed around the hours that matter
Tours.detailItineraryTitle: The itinerary, as it usually runs
Tours.detailItineraryLede: A working draft rather than a fixed schedule — we move days around for weather, festivals and how you are feeling.
Tours.detailEnquireBody: Send us your dates and we will confirm availability, quote precisely, and suggest the two or three changes we would make if it were our own trip.
Tours.detailTailorBody: Quoted individually once we know your dates, lodges and group size.
Tours.detailPriceNote: Final pricing depends on season, room category and group size. No deposit is taken until the itinerary is right.
Tours.detailOtherTitle: You may also be weighing up
Tours.detailCtaText: Altitude, road time, how hard the walking really is, whether the children will cope. Ask us anything — a designer will answer honestly.
Tours.emptyStyle: No journeys in this style yet — but we will design one.
Tours.audience_the_historic_route_for: Travellers who want the classic northern circuit — Lalibela, Gondar, Axum and the Simien rim — at a private pace with boutique lodges and short domestic flights.
Tours.audience_the_historic_route_not: Anyone chasing a cheap fixed group bus tour, or hoping to cover the Danakil and Omo in the same eleven days without rushing.
Tours.audience_simien_escarpment_trek_for: Walkers happy with consecutive days on trail at 3,000–4,200 metres, with mules carrying loads and nights in camp or on the rim.
Tours.audience_simien_escarpment_trek_not: Guests who need paved paths, low altitude, or a lodge every night with no hiking between them.
Tours.audience_omo_valley_immersion_for: Travellers willing to slow down for community-led visits, markets and mediation rather than a photo-stop circuit.
Tours.audience_omo_valley_immersion_not: Anyone expecting pay-per-photo “tribal tourism,” same-day multi-village ticking, or a luxury lodge every night in the lower Omo.
Tours.audience_danakil_expedition_for: Heat-tolerant travellers who accept basic camps, long drives and strict medical and water discipline below sea level.
Tours.audience_danakil_expedition_not: Young children, anyone with serious heart or heat-sensitivity issues, or guests who need hotel comfort throughout.
Tours.audienceTrekFor: Active travellers comfortable with {days} that include real walking, altitude and early starts.
Tours.audienceTrekNot: Guests who prefer purely vehicle-based sightseeing, low elevation, or no trail days at all.
Tours.audienceFamilyFor: Families who want private pacing, sensible road time and rooming that works for children as well as adults.
Tours.audienceFamilyNot: Groups seeking hard multi-day high-altitude treks or extreme lowland heat as the main focus.
Tours.audienceLuxuryFor: Travellers who want private guiding and carefully chosen lodges, with days shaped around light and comfort rather than mileage.
Tours.audienceLuxuryNot: Budget backpackers or guests who want a large fixed group departure at the lowest possible price.
Tours.audienceDefaultFor: Travellers who want a private {days} journey through {places}, reshaped around their pace.
Tours.audienceDefaultNot: Anyone expecting a rigid large-group package that cannot change once booked.
Tours.waysPrivateText: Your own guide, vehicle and dates, with every day shaped around you.
Tours.waysFamilyText: Short drives, family rooms and days that mix one big sight with time to play.
Tours.waysLuxuryText: The finest lodge at every stop, private guides, and nothing rushed.
Tours.waysSmallGroupText: Set departures with other travellers — shared crews, same senior guides.
Tours.waysExpeditionText: Long, demanding journeys: summits, deserts and the far corners of the country.

Destinations.gridTitle: The regions our routes are built from

Destinations.ctaText: A sentence is enough — the altitude you're comfortable with, the pace, roughly when you'd travel. A designer will reply with two or three routes worth considering.

Experiences.heroTitle: Add a day you'll talk about for years
Experiences.heroLede: Short experiences that slot into any journey — in kitchens, coffee houses, farms and villages, on running trails and quiet Rift Valley roads.
Experiences.introTitle: Choose what appeals, and we fit it into your route
Experiences.introBody: Every experience here can be added to any tour or tailor-made journey. Tick the ones you like on the enquiry form — or ask about them once your route takes shape — and we place them where they make sense on the map and in the calendar.
Experiences.longerTitle: Turn an experience into a whole journey
Experiences.ctaTitle: Build your experiences into a journey
Experiences.ctaText: Tell us which experiences caught your eye and roughly when you'd travel. A designer will fit them into a route that makes sense.
Experiences.detailAddBody: Tell us roughly when you're travelling and what else is on your list. We'll fit this in where it works best.

About.heroTitle: A family business, born in Bahir Dar
About.heroLede: Shaped by years on the ground, a love of hospitality, and a lifelong devotion to showing Ethiopia properly.
About.factsBody: Stable details for travellers, partners and anyone checking who we are — the same facts we publish in our structured data.
About.factLabel5: Named for the mountains where it began
About.timelineTitle: From a lakeside town to travellers around the world
About.milestone1Title: A childhood on the shore of Lake Tana
About.milestone1Text: Born and raised in the city where the Blue Nile begins, surrounded by island monasteries and the steady traffic of travellers passing through on their way north.
About.milestone2Text: Weekends and holidays spent working alongside visitors — on the lake, then up on the Simien escarpment. What began alongside school became a calling.
About.milestone3Text: A move to the capital after high school to study Tourism and Tour Operations at the Tourism Training Institute (TTI, formerly CTTI).
About.milestone4Text: Guiding, planning tours, looking after guests and managing destinations for several established operators — learning every side of the work.
About.milestone5Text: A licensed Ethiopian tour company built around private, tailor-made journeys — named for the mountains where it all started.
About.milestone6Text: Operated by three brothers, the wider family and a trusted team of guides and drivers, with the founder still involved in every season from abroad.
About.perspectiveTitle: We know what travellers look for, because we travel too
About.perspectiveBody: Representing the company at tourism fairs and business events, and travelling widely beyond Ethiopia, taught us to see a trip from the guest's side of the table. Five things come up every time.
About.value1Text: Vetted vehicles, experienced drivers, and routes checked against current conditions before every departure.
About.value2Text: Lodges we have stayed in ourselves, and days paced so you arrive rested rather than wrung out.
About.value3Text: Itineraries drawn around light, festivals, altitude and distance — not around what is easiest to sell.
About.value4Text: Straight answers about road time, difficulty and cost, before you book and all the way through.
About.value5Text: The Ethiopian kind — a welcome that begins at the airport and does not switch off when the tour does.
About.teamLaBody: Our founder now lives in the Los Angeles area with family and stays hands-on with every season — which means a conversation in your time zone, with someone who has walked the routes themselves.
About.teamEtBody: Three brothers, the wider family and a trusted team of guides and drivers run every departure from Addis Ababa — the people who meet you at the airport are the people who planned the trip.
About.responsibleTitle: Opening the industry to the people who live here
About.responsibleP1: Tourism gave our family a future, and we want it to do the same for others. We hire locally wherever we travel, and we make a particular point of training and employing women who want to become tour operators and guides.
About.responsibleP2: It is a family story built on experience, opportunity and responsible tourism. Every journey you take with us is a small part of it.
About.ctaTitle: Start a conversation with the family
About.ctaText: Tell us roughly when you'd travel and what draws you to Ethiopia. You'll hear back from one of us — not a call centre.
About.founderQuote: Travel is both my profession and my passion.
About.founderP1: I was born and raised in Bahir Dar, and my life in tourism began there while I was still at school.
About.founderP2: Between classes I worked with visitors in Bahir Dar and up in the Simien Mountains. What started as work alongside my studies became the thing I wanted to do with my life: sharing the cultures, the history, the landscapes and the hospitality of the country I love with people seeing it for the first time.
About.founderP3: After high school I moved to Addis Ababa to study Tourism and Tour Operations at the Tourism Training Institute, then spent years working for other tour companies — guiding, planning itineraries, looking after guests and managing destinations. Those years taught me every side of the work.
About.founderP4: {company} grew out of that. It is a licensed Ethiopian company built for private, tailor-made journeys, and it is run today by my three brothers, our wider family, our team — and me.
